questions.q: When the throne of the Queen of Sheba was set before Solomon, what did he say?
options: “This is the reward of my wisdom”
Not quite. The article says: “This is by the grace of my Lord, to test whether I am grateful or ungrateful”.
“This is by the grace of my Lord, to test whether I am grateful or ungrateful”
Yes. Power is a test, not a prize.
“This proves my kingdom is the greatest”
Not quite. The article says: “This is by the grace of my Lord, to test whether I am grateful or ungrateful”.
“This belongs to my people”
Not quite. The article says: “This is by the grace of my Lord, to test whether I am grateful or ungrateful”.
questions.rationale: “This is by the grace of my Lord, to test whether I am grateful or ungrateful.” (27: 40)

questions.q: The article speaks of two inner forces with which every person is born. What are they, in psychological terms?
options: Instinct and habit
Not quite. The article says: The ego and the conscience.
Hope and fear
Not quite. The article says: The ego and the conscience.
Memory and imagination
Not quite. The article says: The ego and the conscience.
The ego and the conscience
Right. Provoke the ego and it flares; the conscience corrects.
questions.rationale: “In psychological terms, they are the ego and the conscience—with which everyone is born.”

questions.q: What advice did the Prophet give the man who promised to heed it?
options: Consult ten people before acting
Not quite. The article says: Before any action, consider its consequences – go ahead if they are good, refrain if bad.
Act quickly before the chance is lost
Not quite. The article says: Before any action, consider its consequences – go ahead if they are good, refrain if bad.
Before any action, consider its consequences – go ahead if they are good, refrain if bad
Yes. Think before you act.
Do nothing that is new
Not quite. The article says: Before any action, consider its consequences – go ahead if they are good, refrain if bad.
questions.rationale: “When you decide on some action, think of its consequences. If they are good, go ahead with it: and if they are bad, refrain from it.”

questions.q: What, according to the article, did most to move Western study of Islam towards objectivity?
options: The scientific method, which made a subjective colouring of history unacceptable
Well read. An interdependent world helped too.
The opening of new trade routes
Not quite. The article says: The scientific method, which made a subjective colouring of history unacceptable.
The invention of printing
Not quite. The article says: The scientific method, which made a subjective colouring of history unacceptable.
The decline of universities
Not quite. The article says: The scientific method, which made a subjective colouring of history unacceptable.
questions.rationale: “A great factor that helped to promote this trend was the development of science. Science has given a new method of study that is completely objective.”

questions.article: Complaints Take You Away from God
questions.q: A person wrongly deprived may receive far more from God than was taken. On what condition, says the article?
options: That he leaves his town for good
Not quite. The article says: That he stays free of complaint, remains hopeful of God, and wishes his oppressors well.
That he demands his rights loudly
Not quite. The article says: That he stays free of complaint, remains hopeful of God, and wishes his oppressors well.
That he repays the wrong in kind
Not quite. The article says: That he stays free of complaint, remains hopeful of God, and wishes his oppressors well.
That he stays free of complaint, remains hopeful of God, and wishes his oppressors well
Correct. Positivity despite negative experience.
questions.rationale: “This eligibility is that in such conditions he remains, till the final limit, a non-complaining person.”

questions.q: During a drought, merchants offered Usman high prices for his caravan of grain. What “better price” did he choose?
options: A higher bid from Syria
Not quite. The article says: God’s tenfold reward – he gave it all to the needy.
A share in the merchants’ future trade
Not quite. The article says: God’s tenfold reward – he gave it all to the needy.
Payment in gold instead of silver
Not quite. The article says: God’s tenfold reward – he gave it all to the needy.
God’s tenfold reward – he gave it all to the needy
Yes. Faith in God’s promise made the sacrifice easy.
questions.rationale: “‘I can get ten dirhams for every one dirhams worth,’ he told them… Then he told them that he was giving all the goods to the needy people of Madinah.”

questions.q: A pilot saw another aircraft on a collision course and dived three hundred feet. What lesson does the article draw?
options: The lower course is always safer
Not quite. The article says: Sometimes stepping back is wiser than pressing forward; avoidance saves both sides.
Sometimes stepping back is wiser than pressing forward; avoidance saves both sides
Well reasoned. Retreat can be the real success.
Flying is too dangerous
Not quite. The article says: Sometimes stepping back is wiser than pressing forward; avoidance saves both sides.
Instructions should not be trusted
Not quite. The article says: Sometimes stepping back is wiser than pressing forward; avoidance saves both sides.
questions.rationale: “Just as advancing is necessary to succeed in life, so is retreating… When there is fear of a head-on collision, avoidance is the only solution.”

questions.q: Hans Bethe told his wife she was standing beside the only person who knew why the stars shine. What does the article say this joy should teach a believer?
options: The discovery of God is far greater, and one who has truly made it will feel and share its thrill
Right. No joy means the discovery is not yet made.
Scientists are proud people
Not quite. The article says: The discovery of God is far greater, and one who has truly made it will feel and share its thrill.
Knowledge should be kept to oneself
Not quite. The article says: The discovery of God is far greater, and one who has truly made it will feel and share its thrill.
Stars are less wonderful once explained
Not quite. The article says: The discovery of God is far greater, and one who has truly made it will feel and share its thrill.
questions.rationale: “Those who really believe in God feel the thrill of their discovery… If there are no traces of the joy of discovery, the discovery itself has yet to be made.”

questions.q: Steel and atomic energy lay harmless in nature for ages. Why did they become destructive in human hands?
options: Scientists made mistakes in calculation
Not quite. The article says: Man is free, and weapons are a misuse of that freedom – freedom is a test, not a right.
Nature’s materials changed over time
Not quite. The article says: Man is free, and weapons are a misuse of that freedom – freedom is a test, not a right.
There were too few resources to share
Not quite. The article says: Man is free, and weapons are a misuse of that freedom – freedom is a test, not a right.
Man is free, and weapons are a misuse of that freedom – freedom is a test, not a right
Exactly. Self-discipline, not freedom alone, brings peace.
questions.rationale: “The reason is that nature has no freedom. Man, on the other hand, is free to act as he pleases… The freedom of choice that man has been given in the world today is a test; it is not his right.”

questions.q: “Always measure with justice and do not give short measure.” How does the commentary connect this with the universe?
options: The universe runs on balance and justice, and man is asked to weigh his words and deeds by the same standard
Well read. The Quran states it; the cosmos shows it.
Traders alone are addressed
Not quite. The article says: The universe runs on balance and justice, and man is asked to weigh his words and deeds by the same standard.
Justice is possible only in the next world
Not quite. The article says: The universe runs on balance and justice, and man is asked to weigh his words and deeds by the same standard.
The universe is too vast to be measured
Not quite. The article says: The universe runs on balance and justice, and man is asked to weigh his words and deeds by the same standard.
questions.rationale: “The whole world surrounding the human being is based on these principles of balance and justice, which God wants human beings to follow.”
